subject: Lyra Labs dedicated fit: token run-rate, headroom and tail-latency modeling

Subject: Dedicated fit questions — latency & run-rate for Lyra conversation flow

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our platform team is trying to map the Dedicated commitment to the performance envelope we'll need. We have two main production surfaces:

- Short responses (avg 60 tokens) for intent classification and quick replies (heavy traffic)
- Conversational completion path (avg 420 tokens) for the main assistant (medium traffic, latency-sensitive)

Rough traffic profile (peak): ~1800 requests/minute for short responses, ~120 requests/minute for completions. We expect a growth runway of ~30% over 12 months.

Two asks for your modeling:
1) For our 95th percentile latency SLO of 200ms for short responses (60 tokens) and 450ms for completions (420 tokens), what token/sec numbers should we map to a Dedicated commit?
2) What headroom multiplier do you recommend for burst tolerance and autoscaling (we want to avoid tail latency blips during feature launches)?

I've attached a small sample of the traffic shape (CSV) — can you review and propose GPU sizing + rough cost guidance?

Thanks,
Emma

--
Emma Black
Head of Platform
Lyra Labs

Subject: Re: Dedicated fit questions — latency & run-rate for Lyra conversation flow

Emma —

Appreciate the sample and the clear SLOs. High-level read: your peak tokens/sec requirement based on the numbers you sent is roughly 1,740 tokens/sec (short + completion blended) today, before growth. Quick calc I used:
- Short path: 1800 req/min * 60 tokens = 108k tokens/min = 1,800 tokens/sec
- Completion path: 120 req/min * 420 tokens = 50.4k tokens/min = 840 tokens/sec
Blended instantaneous peak = 1,800 + 840 = 2,640 tokens/sec, but note short responses are much easier to batch and hit lower latency.

What we recommend as a conservative committed baseline (to meet your 95th P99-ish SLO targets):
- Baseline committed throughput: 2,700 tokens/sec steady-state
- Burst/headroom target: 1.6x for short-term bursts (=> ~4,320 tps)
- Safety cushion for launch & growth (12 months): 1.3x multiplier on committed baseline

That implies: committed floor ~2,700 tps, nominal planning envelope for capacity ops ~2,700 * 1.3 * 1.6 ≈ 5,644 tps (this is the runway we should be able to handle without emergency fallbacks).

Modeling assumptions I used (attached workbook summarizes):
- Serving model: GPT-style 7B+/13B family quantized to int8 (we tested on your sample traces).
- Average generation cost scales linearly with tokens; we assume KV cache hit rates of 12% for conversational flow.
- Batching windows: 10–15ms default at high concurrency; small-path responses often use micro-batching (2–6ms queues).

Next steps I propose: Ben will follow up with per-GPU throughput estimates (H100 / A100), and Marissa will generate a committed quote with slab sizing and pricing tiers for the ranges above.

Attaching your CSV back and a quick model-fit workbook so you can see the sensitivity table.

Regards,
Vivek

Subject: Re: Dedicated fit questions — latency & run-rate for Lyra conversation flow

Emma / team —

Sharing the hardware-level breakdown and numbers I ran from our internal benchmark harness (note: these are conservative - real can improve with tuned kernels):

Assumptions
- Model family: Redwood-13B-ish equivalent, quantized to int8 for inference
- Typical output length considered for bench: 420 tokens (completion path) and 60 tokens (short path)
- Latency SLO targets: 95th <= 450ms (completions), 95th <= 200ms (short)

Per-GPU sustained token throughput (approx):
- H100 80GB (int8): 6,500 tokens/sec per GPU (completion mix, with batching turned on)
- A100 80GB (fp16/int8 mixed): 3,200 tokens/sec per GPU

Sizing notes
- Baseline committed (2,700 tps):
  - H100 plan: 2 GPUs (sustained 13k tps capacity) gives you steady headroom and room for rolling upgrades; cost-optimized plan would route to a 1.6x burst zone via autoscale to another 1 GPU (3 total) for brief spikes.
  - A100 plan: 1x A100 minimum doesn't meet baseline; recommended 2–3 A100s (3 gives ~9.6k tps) to match headroom profile.

Tail-latency and SLO fit
- To meet 95th P latency: ensure micro-batch sizes are small for the short path (we push batching timeouts to 3–6ms).
- We suggest a KV prefix cache for repeated context to reduce compute on conversational tails (saves ~10–20% of token compute across traces).
- With H100 & int8 + caching, simulated 95th lat for 60-token path: ~110–140ms; for 420-token path: ~260–380ms depending on burst mixing and network hop times.

Operational recommendations
- Canary: 1 GPU in your VPC (H100) for a 2-week canary, route 5–10% traffic and use the same prompt sets.
- Autoscaling policy: scale by CPU-based queue depth + token backlog metric; target to spin an extra GPU when backlog > 8k tokens for >30s.

I'll attach the raw benchmark logs separately if you want the per-run traces.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Customer Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
